records.title: Kinetic Foundry
records.prompt:
Create a single-page landing page for **KINETIC FOUNDRY**, a fictional industrial robotics company that builds modular robotic work cells for small and mid-sized manufacturers.

Use the supplied SYSTEM//FORM skill as the governing design system.

### Required content

**KINETIC FOUNDRY**

**Automation built for factories that change.**

Modular robotic work cells designed to be reconfigured as production demands evolve.

**KF / CELL 04**

Payload: 35 kg  
Reach: 1,850 mm  
Repeatability: ±0.05 mm  
Configuration: 6-axis  
Deployment: Modular

Include:

- hero
- product overview
- technical specifications
- three capabilities
- deployment/process section
- final contact CTA

### Direction

Do not imitate a conventional robotics or SaaS website.

The product and its real specifications should become part of the visual architecture.

Use technical graphics only where they communicate actual supplied information.

Do not invent additional specifications, certifications, performance claims, customers, statistics, coordinates, or operational data.

### Evaluation target

This is SYSTEM//FORM operating on its natural subject matter.

The result should demonstrate the design system without relying on generic futuristic, cyberpunk, or industrial-tech tropes.

records.title: Northline Coffee
records.prompt:
Create a single-page website for **NORTHLINE COFFEE**, a fictional independent specialty coffee roaster.

Use the supplied SYSTEM//FORM skill as the governing design system.

### Required content

**NORTHLINE COFFEE**

**Coffee with a known origin.**

Featured release:

**LAS FLORES / 04**

Origin: Huila, Colombia  
Producer: Las Flores  
Process: Washed  
Variety: Caturra  
Altitude: 1,850 MASL  
Roast: Light

Tasting notes:

Red apple / caramel / citrus

Include:

- hero
- featured coffee
- origin information
- roasting philosophy
- three available coffee offerings
- shop CTA

For the other two coffee offerings, use clearly marked placeholder content rather than inventing factual origins or specifications.

### Direction

Do not make the company feel industrial.

Do not use factory, machine, robotics, diagnostic, system-status, engineering, or manufacturing language simply to satisfy the design style.

Find SYSTEM//FORM inside the **real informational structure of coffee**: origin, process, variety, altitude, roast, product, and provenance.

Avoid generic specialty-coffee minimalism.

### Evaluation target

If SYSTEM//FORM is truly transferable, this should remain recognizably SYSTEM//FORM while feeling unquestionably like a coffee brand.

records.title: Great Lakes Industrial Archive
records.prompt:
Create a homepage for **THE GREAT LAKES INDUSTRIAL ARCHIVE**, a fictional nonprofit archive preserving documents, photographs, oral histories, and physical artifacts related to Great Lakes manufacturing history.

Use the supplied SYSTEM//FORM skill as the governing design system.

### Required content

**THE GREAT LAKES INDUSTRIAL ARCHIVE**

**Industry remembered through the people who built it.**

Collections:

Photographs — 18,420 records  
Documents — 7,860 records  
Oral Histories — 614 records  
Physical Objects — 1,205 records

Established: 1987

Include:

- institutional hero
- collection overview
- featured archive object
- research/access information
- preservation mission
- visit/contact CTA

Use placeholder labeling for any featured object's details that have not been supplied.

### Direction

Use SYSTEM mode as the primary expression.

This should feel scholarly, archival, contemporary, and authoritative—not like robotics branding.

Avoid excessive signal colors, fake measurements, machinery diagrams, fake catalog identifiers, and unnecessary technical decoration.

Allow typography, information organization, proportion, rules, and negative space to carry most of the identity.

### Evaluation target

This tests whether SYSTEM//FORM can become restrained without disappearing.

records.title: COMMON GROUND
records.prompt:
Create a complete fictional website for:

# COMMON GROUND

Regional Food Cooperative

Apply the supplied **LOOM — Woven Systems Design Skill**.

This project should test whether LOOM can organize a large regional food ecosystem without turning into:

- a farmer's-market website
- rustic branding
- Main Street nostalgia
- a directory of cards
- a farm-to-table cliché
- an infographic network diagram

## CORE CONCEPT

The website should feel like:

> **"A region's growers, makers, kitchens, markets, seasons, and food all occupy one shared field."**

COMMON GROUND is a member-owned cooperative connecting:

- vegetable farms
- orchards
- bakers
- grain growers
- dairies
- preserves
- restaurants
- small grocers
- weekly markets
- seasonal subscriptions

The identity should feel:

- regional
- contemporary
- useful
- abundant
- cooperative
- grounded
- editorial
- optimistic
- specific

Do not use weaving vocabulary in the public-facing copy.

The visual structure, not the words, should carry the metaphor.

## STRUCTURAL IDEA

Establish four recurring content families:

**GROW**

**MAKE**

**SELL**

**SHARE**

These are **not four permanent visible columns**.

They are recurring structural roles that can occupy changing spans across the page.

A grower story may begin narrow and expand into a broad image field.

A market notice may sit compactly near the page edge.

A recipe may cross content that originated in GROW and MAKE without drawing literal connecting lines.

## OPENING FIELD

Possible headline:

# Good food is a regional practice.

Supporting copy:

COMMON GROUND brings farms, makers, kitchens, markets, and neighbors into one cooperative food system.

Create a composition including:

- broad seasonal produce photography
- cooperative statement
- current season
- next market
- member count
- shop / join action

Do not place these facts inside statistic cards.

Use span and adjacency.

## 01 / THIS WEEK

Create a dense current-availability field.

Possible items:

- Early Girl Tomatoes
- Sweet Corn
- Okra
- Sourdough
- Stone-Ground Grits
- Peach Preserves
- Cultured Butter
- Blueberries
- Summer Squash

Group by practical availability but do not create a standard ecommerce product grid.

Mix:

- narrow product strips
- one broader feature product
- compact prices
- producer name
- availability state

Example:

**Sweet Corn**

Benton Ridge Farm

$7 / dozen

SATURDAY MARKET

The section should use **tight tension**.

## 02 / PRODUCER FIELD

Feature several fictional producers:

**Benton Ridge Farm**

**Hollow Creek Dairy**

**West Fork Milling**

**Morrow Orchard**

**Beck & Sons Bakery**

Use:

- portraits or work photography
- landscape crops
- product detail
- short producer statements

Do not create five matching profile cards.

Let some producers occupy only a strip while one receives a broad feature band.

## 03 / SEASON

Create a seasonal section for:

# LATE SUMMER

Show a changing rhythm of:

- harvest
- market
- storage
- kitchen
- preserve

Allow the composition to become more open here.

Use loose tension and broad imagery.

No generic seasonal iconography.

## 04 / MARKET

Create practical current information:

**SATURDAY MARKET**

8 AM–1 PM

Riverside Hall

46 vendors this week

Include:

- featured vendors
- pickup window
- market map link
- payment information
- accessibility information

This should remain highly useful.

Do not let the design concept reduce clarity.

## 05 / COOPERATIVE STORY

Explain:

records.title: AERA
records.prompt:
Create a fully designed, responsive sample website whose purpose is to showcase and stress-test a design skill system rather than serve a real client.

This is not a generic business website. It is a visual demonstration site that explores the design language, component system, layout grammar, graphic treatments, and reusable primitives of the skill.

Use the following setup:

DESIGN SKILL:
[INSERT SKILL NAME OR ATTACH SKILL FILE]

OPTIONAL GRAPHIC PRIMITIVE:
[INSERT GRAPHIC PRIMITIVE NAME, such as Contour Field]
If included, integrate it as a compositional element or graphic effect, not as a gimmick. It must support the brand and layout rather than dominate them.

SITE GOAL:
Build a single-page showcase site that lets me quickly evaluate:
- the overall aesthetic of the skill
- how the skill handles hierarchy and layout
- the component styling
- how the graphic primitive behaves in real compositions
- the flexibility of the system across different section types
- whether the design feels like a usable web system rather than a one-off mockup

IMPORTANT:
This is a “style and system demo” site. It should feel polished, intentional, and realistic, but it does not need to represent a real company. Use a fictional but believable brand or concept that fits the design language.

The output should be a complete front-end prototype in HTML/CSS/JS if needed.

CORE REQUIREMENTS

1. Build a strong homepage-style experience with multiple varied sections that showcase the skill in action.

2. Include a fictional brand name, short positioning statement, and believable sample content. Do not use lorem ipsum. Use concise, tasteful copy that supports the visual presentation.

3. The design should showcase a full visual system, including:
- navigation / header
- hero section
- section transitions
- typography hierarchy
- buttons and links
- cards
- feature grid
- stats or metrics
- media/image blocks
- testimonials or quotes
- CTA section
- footer

4. Include a dedicated “system showcase” or “design lab” section that clearly demonstrates:
- heading styles
- body text
- buttons
- form inputs
- cards
- list styles
- icon treatment if appropriate
- color usage
- spacing rhythm
- dividers / rules / overlays
- surface/background variations

5. If a graphic primitive is included, demonstrate it in multiple ways across the page, such as:
- subtle hero background
- corner or edge field
- section bleed
- masked text or object fill
- object halo
- cutaway around important content
- divider treatment
Use restraint. The primitive should feel integrated, not pasted everywhere.

6. Show range across sections. Some sections can be:
- calm and minimal
- dense and editorial
- structured and grid-based
- atmospheric and spacious
- more promotional or conversion-oriented

7. The page should help answer:
“What does this skill look like in practice?”
“What kinds of compositions does it support?”
“Does it feel flexible?”
“What reusable visual moves define it?”

8. Make it feel like a polished concept demo, not a wireframe and not a random AI collage.

9. Keep the design system coherent. Repetition should feel intentional. Variation should happen within the rules of the skill.

10. Responsiveness matters. The design should adapt well to desktop and mobile, preserving hierarchy and clarity.

DESIGN BEHAVIOR

- Prioritize composition, hierarchy, and visual rhythm.
- Let the brand identity shine through the system.
- Do not let decorative effects overwhelm readability.
- Avoid default SaaS-template sameness unless the skill specifically calls for it.
- Avoid filler sections that exist only to increase page length.
- Make each section reveal something useful about the system.

STRUCTURE TO INCLUDE

At minimum, include sections like:
1. Header / nav
2. Hero
3. Brand intro or positioning section
4. Features / capabilities grid
5. Showcase section with cards or case-study style blocks
6. System showcase / design lab section
7. Metrics / stats section
8. Testimonial or quote section
9. CTA section
10. Footer

OPTIONAL ADVANCED SECTIONS
Add any that help demonstrate the skill:
- editorial split section
- timeline
- comparison table
- featured article block
- gallery strip
- layered content panel
- large pull quote
- process section
- FAQ accordion
- sticky side navigation
- experimental visual section

VISUAL QUALITY BAR

I want this to feel like a deliberate, curated design exploration.
It should look like something created to evaluate and present the strength of the skill.
The result should feel like a mini design system demo site, not just a homepage for a fake startup.

OUTPUT EXPECTATION

Produce the implementation directly.
Use semantic HTML and organized CSS.
Use light JS only if needed.
Make the prototype visually polished and presentation-ready.

records.title: Squish
records.prompt:
Build a brand site for a fictional gummy candy brand called "Squish", as a demo of the Candy branch of our claymorphism design skill. Apply the skill at ~/workspace/skills/webstyle-claymorphism/SKILL.md, Candy branch.
Tokens and rules: warm cream (#FDF6EC) page base; blush pink (#FFD6E0), butter yellow (#FFE29A), sky blue (#BDE0FE), mint green (#CAE9C9) as the candy palette; clay brown (#C4A27E) for grounding accents. Soft toy-like 3D clay surfaces, huge corner radii, the signature triple-shadow stack (tinted outer drop shadow + soft inner top highlight + inner bottom shade), matte grain-free surfaces, springy playful composition, airy low-density layouts. Rounded sans typography (Nunito / Quicksand spirit), generous line-height. No sharp corners, no hard shadows, no neon.
Imagery — two generated images are ready as local files; integrate them (copy or reference as the build requires):
Hero: /home/hatch/workspace/squish-assets/media-generation-squish-hero-0-<uuid>.webp — a joyful tumble of giant puffy clay gummy candies; anchor the hero with it.
Mascot: /home/hatch/workspace/squish-assets/media-generation-squish-mascot-0-<uuid>.webp — the round clay gummy-bear mascot; feature it in a brand/mascot section.
Content (invent sweet, playful copy): hero with the candy tumble, flavor lineup cards (each flavor a puffy clay tile), the mascot's story section, a "squish test" interactive texture note, shop teaser with prices, newsletter signup ("get the drop"). Tone: joyful, chewy, kid-at-heart but design-literate.
Fully responsive; at 390px the clay tiles stack in a single column, radii stay huge, nothing overflows horizontally.
